{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABWDVChw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzg_mEy4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 77, "title": "Redesign Chrome extension UI into Live, Graph Editor, and Models screens", "body": "## Problem

The Chrome extension's recorder window currently mixes live transcription, paired translation results, an embedded visual processing-graph editor, OPUS-MT download/cache controls and TTS download/cache controls in one narrow page. The UI is difficult to scan, visually inconsistent, and cumbersome for everyday transcription. Graph editing needs a larger canvas, while model management belongs in one discoverable place.

We want a coherent, modern, usable interface without rewriting or changing the local ASR, translation, TTS or Pipeline implementations.

## Expected outcome

Reorganize the unpacked Chrome extension into **three clearly navigable surfaces** with a restrained, consistent dark-oriented visual design:

1. **Live — recording and results:** the primary, compact recorder window focused on current-tab status, Start/Stop/Cancel, copyable transcription, and paired source/translation history. Show completed utterances in order, original and translated text together, and the current provisional original/translation distinctly. A concise model-unavailable message should link to the Models screen instead of burying users in settings. Keep optional generated-audio playback/WAV controls available when the saved graph includes TTS.
2. **Graph Editor — separate full-size tab/page:** move the existing executable graph editor out of the recorder's narrow disclosure panel. Use a discoverable node palette, broad scrollable/zoomable canvas with visible typed ports and wires, and a settings inspector for the selected Node. Support existing add/remove, move, connect/disconnect, validate, save/load/reset behavior. Show the difference between unsaved draft, saved next-session graph and running active graph. Editing a graph must never silently mutate an active Pipeline.
3. **Models — consolidated model manager:** move the real OPUS-MT (ja→en, en→ja) and TTS (Supertonic 3, Kokoro) preparation/cache controls to a dedicated page/tab accessible from Live and Graph Editor. Show per-model verified Cached/Ready, Not downloaded, Downloading progress, Error/retry and deletion where supported. ReazonSpeech/Silero bundled assets should be labeled **Bundled**, not pretend to have the same optional download lifecycle. Model sizes, direction/voice where applicable, licenses/terms and best-effort Chrome-profile persistence must remain clear. Do not mistake the existing tiny #67 cache fixture for a real installed model.

### Design goals

- Consistent spacing, typography, contrast, buttons, navigation and status treatment; support dark appearance without sacrificing legibility or reduced-motion/keyboard accessibility.
- Prioritize Live as the most frequent task; avoid presenting the entire graph/model-download configuration during an ordinary recording.
- Give Graph Editor usable width and discoverable port connections rather than merely restyling its existing embedded widget.
- Use current extension state as the source of truth. No decorative or fake "Ready"/"LIVE" indicators or fabricated translation output.
- Preserve the current toolbar-driven popup-window capture model; opening editor or model-manager tabs must **not** implicitly start/stop/retarget capture.

## Scope

- Reuse the existing `extension/graph.js`, `graph-runtime.js`, `graph-editor.js`, `model-asset-cache.js`, OPUS-MT and TTS caches, `TabSession` and production Pipeline/Nodes. Keep the persisted graph format compatible with #75 and migrate existing preferences only if actually necessary.
- Create separate extension-origin Graph Editor and Models pages (or evolve the existing options page) and small, clear navigation from the Live recorder. Ensure page URLs, scripts and packaged files work under MV3 CSP without remote executable code or new permissions unless strictly justified.
- Preserve the selected saved graph and settings across extension windows/pages and Chrome restarts in the same profile. Make draft-vs-saved updates and cross-page refresh behavior explicit; do not silently overwrite newer edits. No need for a speculative sync service or UI framework.
- Preserve actual transcription behavior, status/error diagnostics, original/provisional/final pairing and ordering, both OPUS-MT directions, download/retry, TTS playback/WAV, Stop/finalize, Cancel, tab capture and audio playback restoration.
- Model preparation remains explicitly user-initiated. If cache state is missing/evicted, give a targeted recovery action; neither opening the Models page nor enabling a saved graph should silently download hundreds of MB. Preserve clear progress/error/status and cancellation.
- Keep TranslateGemma **unavailable** in the extension unless independently validated; do not add inference/model functionality as part of this UI issue. No new Node framework or external service.
- Update user documentation and lightweight UI test fixtures/screenshots as needed. Focus on usability/layout rather than re-architecting inference.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- Opening a tab's toolbar action displays a **compact Live UI** with working Start/Stop/Cancel, active audio/capture status, legible ordered original/translation final rows, clearly marked provisional rows, copying of final text, and existing optional TTS audio controls when configured.
- Live provides working navigation to a **separate wide Graph Editor page** and **Models page**. Navigating to either does not interfere with an active tab-capture session or start additional capture/inference.
- Editor supports actual typed-port drag/click connections, node placement, settings, validation feedback, save/load/reset, and retains exact executable graph behavior. Saved changes apply only on a new session; all existing saved/default graphs and language preferences continue to work.
- Models shows actual cache readiness separately for ReazonSpeech (bundled), both OPUS-MT models, and both TTS models; supports explicit download, progress, retry, cancellation, and removal of optional assets when supported, without false ready statuses or redundant model stores.
- A previously cached complete model remains recognizable after page recreation and Chrome-profile restart; eviction/incomplete assets show missing state and actionable retry instead of a misleading status.
- Accessibility basics verified: keyboard-reachable navigation and editor port actions, labeled controls, visible focus, useful status/alert semantics, readable narrow/wide window layouts, and no essential meaning conveyed only by color.
- MV3 extension browser tests cover navigation, active-session preservation during editor/models use, real graph execution from a saved edit, per-model preparation/errors/retry, and draft vs. active state. Existing unit/browser/extension tests and packaging pass. Use deterministic model fixtures for routine UI tests; do not claim they prove full model inference. Record any real-model checks separately.
- The UI does not require additional unnecessary extension permissions or remote JS/CSS, and no user speech/text leaves the local inference flow.

## Required post-merge verification

None specific to an unpacked Chrome extension. Chrome Web Store release or public site changes are not in scope. Any actual release-only verification must be recorded separately and not claimed passed based on pre-merge tests.

## Context

- #75 — executable visual graph editor with saved configurations; `docs/extension-graph.md`.
- #67, #69, #71 — model cache, live/final translation and selectable direction.
- #73 — Supertonic 3/Kokoro local TTS Nodes.
- `extension/recorder.html`, `extension/recorder.js`, `extension/graph-editor.js`, `extension/model-cache.html`, `docs/chrome-extension.md`.
- UX inspirations: **Otter.ai** for readable transcription and paired conversation history; **n8n** and **React Flow** for a spacious node editor, node palette and selection inspector. These are **references for layout/interactions only**, not a mandate to adopt those products' libraries.

Do not close this Issue with a static mockup or CSS-only refresh: the three screens, navigation and working real controls are the deliverable.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/77", "created_at": "2026-10-09T07:56:19Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/my-audio-to-text", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "81a1ef63b1e3406c92725ba69410b81f"}
